question: 监控为什么总是朝下查？
question_en: Why does scrutiny always run downhill?
sub: 被查的总是位置更低的那一方——这项核查，能不能反过来施加给提出它的人？
sub_en: The one who gets checked is always the one lower down — could this check be turned around on whoever proposed it?

casting.reason: 核查在他这里不是上位者的特权，而是没有背景的人对付任人唯亲的工具：没有公开的标准，胜出的永远是有关系、有出身的那一个。他要的是一把两头都量的尺——法仪既然是尺，就不能只量下面。他之所以坚持鬼神确实能赏善罚暴，用意也很实际：人间的刑罚够不着最有权势的人，那就得给他们头顶也安一双不受贿的眼睛。
casting.reason_en: For him, verification is not a privilege of those above but the tool by which people without connections fight nepotism: where there is no public standard, the winner is always whoever has the right family and the right friends. What he wants is a measure that reads both ends — if the standard is a ruler, it cannot be laid only against those below. His insistence that spirits really do reward the good and punish the violent has a practical point too: human punishment cannot reach the most powerful, so a pair of unbribable eyes has to be installed above their heads as well.

casting.reason: 他不信任何一把尺子能保持干净：造出斗斛来量，大盗连斗斛一起偷走；写下仁义来劝善，篡国者反倒把仁义供在自家门下。窃钩的被处死，窃国的做了诸侯——他要指出的不是刑罚有漏洞，而是规则会随着盗取的规模改换主人。对被量的人，他给的不是抗议而是保全：留一块无人考核的地方，别把自己削成能填进表格的形状。
casting.reason_en: He trusts no measure to stay clean: make a bushel to measure with and the great thief steals the bushel along with the grain; write down benevolence to encourage virtue and the man who seizes a state ends up enshrining benevolence at his own gate. The one who steals a belt-hook is executed, the one who steals a state becomes a lord — his point is not that punishment has loopholes but that rules change owners according to the scale of the theft. To those being measured he offers not protest but preservation: keep one corner of your life that nobody assesses, and do not whittle yourself into a shape that fits the form.

casting.reason: 在他看来，核查的目的从来不是查明真相，而是造出一种随时准备好被查看的人。环形监狱的关键不在塔里有没有看守，而在你无法确定——不确定得久了，人就自己接手了看守的活。所以他反对把『双向监控』当解药：把透明铺满每一个人，规训只会更完整。他更在意一个没人问出口的问题：为什么在今天，信任非得以留痕的形式才被承认。
casting.reason_en: Verification, as he sees it, was never about establishing the truth; it is about producing a person who is permanently ready to be looked at. What matters in the circular prison is not whether a guard is in the tower but that you cannot know — and after long enough uncertainty, people take over the guard's job themselves. Hence his refusal to treat mutual surveillance as the cure: spread transparency across everyone and discipline only becomes more complete. What interests him more is a question nobody asks aloud: why, in our time, must trust take the form of a record before it counts.

casting.reason: 核查是一件要花钱的消费，在他眼里这几乎就是全部解释：谁付得起，谁就用得上，所以它当然只从上往下流。但他给上位者的忠告不带一丝道德——只查下、从不受查的君主，收到的每一份报表都是别人算准了他会看才写下的，久而久之他被自己的眼睛蒙住。他因此主张自愿交出一部分核查权，理由不是善良，是想听见真话。
casting.reason_en: Verification is something you have to pay for, and in his eyes that is very nearly the whole explanation: whoever can afford it uses it, so of course it only ever flows downward. But the counsel he offers those above carries no morality at all — a prince who inspects everyone and is inspected by none receives reports written by people who have calculated exactly what he will read, and in time he is blinded by his own eyes. So he argues for surrendering part of that power voluntarily, not out of goodness but because he wants to hear the truth.

casting.reason: 在企业里他看到的因果恰好倒过来：监控不是权力的产物，而是管理失败留下的补丁。说不清下属该交出什么成果的经理，只能退而去数动作——登录时长、消息条数、工位上的人头。他提出的目标管理，后半截『与自我控制』常被人略掉，而那才是重点：能自己检验成效的人，本来就不需要被盯着。
casting.reason_en: Inside a company he sees the causation running the other way: monitoring is not a product of power but a patch left behind by failed management. A manager who cannot say what results a subordinate owes is left counting motions instead — hours logged in, messages sent, heads at desks. The second half of his own phrase, management by objectives *and self-control*, is the part people drop, and it is the part that matters: someone who can check their own results never needed watching in the first place.

casting.reason: 他带来的是两边都不讨好的证据。一边，控制会挤走善意：被设了下限的人，交出的努力反而少于完全没被设限时。另一边，把监督整个撤掉也不行，公共品实验里的合作率会一路滑到接近零。而他最不愿意承认的那个结果是：一旦允许被罚的人反过来报复，合作反而崩溃——有效的制裁往往正是不对称的制裁。
casting.reason_en: The evidence he brings satisfies neither side. On one hand, control crowds out goodwill: people given a minimum requirement return less effort than people given none at all. On the other, removing oversight entirely does not work either — in public goods experiments cooperation slides towards zero. And the finding he least wants to concede is this: once those who are punished may retaliate against the punisher, cooperation collapses. Sanctions that work are often precisely the asymmetric ones.

casting.reason: 被监控的代价，在他那里是可以量出来的。白厅研究里一万多名公务员，人人有工作、有医保，死亡率却随职级呈连续的梯度往下掉，而抽烟、血压、胆固醇加起来只解释得了其中一小部分。他把矛头指向掌控感：要求高、裁量小，正是长期被核查的人所处的位置。所以他不肯让话题停在怎样查得更聪明，而要追问这项核查有没有把决定权还回去一点。
casting.reason_en: In his hands the cost of being watched becomes measurable. Among the ten thousand-odd civil servants of the Whitehall studies — all employed, all covered by health care — mortality still fell in a continuous gradient with rank, and smoking, blood pressure and cholesterol together explained only a small part of it. He points instead at control: high demand with little discretion is exactly the position of someone under long-term scrutiny. So he refuses to let the conversation settle on how to inspect more cleverly, and asks instead whether a given inspection hands any decision back.

posts.text: 别把这当成偏心。核查从来不是为了知道真相，而是为了造出一种人：知道自己随时可能被看，于是自己看住自己。边沁那座 panopticon 的妙处不在塔里有人，而在你永远无法确定塔里有没有人——**权力最省钱的形式，是让被看的人自己接手看守的工作。**所以监控当然朝下：可见性就是位置本身。上位者的特权不是不被查，而是**不必被看见**。你们等一下多半会提议『双向监控』，我先说在前面：对称的透明不解放任何人，它只会把规训铺得更满。
posts.text_en: Do not mistake this for favouritism. Verification was never about knowing the truth; it is about manufacturing a certain kind of person — one who knows they might be looked at any moment, and so keeps watch over themselves. The genius of Bentham's panopticon is not that someone is in the tower but that you can never be sure whether anyone is. **The cheapest form power has ever found is to hand the job of guarding over to the guarded.** Of course scrutiny runs downhill: visibility is position. The privilege of those above is not that they escape inspection but that **they need not be seen at all**. Someone will shortly propose mutual surveillance, so let me say it first: symmetrical transparency liberates nobody. It only spreads discipline more evenly.

glossary.panopticon: panopticon（全景敞视监狱）：边沁 1787 年设计的环形监狱——中央一座瞭望塔，四周牢房全部朝内敞开，看守能看见每一间，囚犯却看不见塔里有没有人。我借它说明现代权力：真正起作用的不是持续的观看，而是被看的不确定性；久了，人就替看守站了岗。
glossary.规训: discipline（规训）：我用来指近代学校、军队、医院、工厂共有的那套技术——把人分格安置、排定时刻表、规定动作标准、反复考核并留下记录。它不靠威吓，而靠细密的日常纠正，把人塑造成可预测、可比较、可管理的个体。

glossary_en.panopticon: The circular prison Bentham designed in 1787: a watchtower at the centre, cells arranged around it and open to the inside, so the guard sees every cell while no prisoner can see whether anyone is in the tower. I use it to describe modern power — what does the work is not continuous observation but uncertainty about it; given time, people stand the watch themselves.
glossary_en.discipline: My term for the techniques shared by the modern school, army, hospital and factory: partitioning people in space, imposing timetables, specifying the correct movement, examining repeatedly and writing it all down. It does not threaten; it corrects in small daily increments, until individuals emerge who are predictable, comparable and manageable.

posts.text: 察之朝下，非独今之弊也。上不受法而独以法绳下，是执法者自外于法也。**法仪者，两端俱量之器，不可但量其下。**世人笑吾明鬼，然吾之所以明鬼者，正为使贵者亦有所畏：吏之不肖，民得而察之；君之不肖，谁察之？故必托之天鬼。然察终不可废——不察，则亲亲相举，贤者终身不得进，此吾言尚贤之所以难也。**故察之正与不正，在其法能否反加于立法之人。**
posts.text_en: That inspection runs downward is not a fault of our age alone. When those above stand outside the law and use it only to bind those below, the enforcer has placed himself beyond his own rule. **A standard is an instrument that measures at both ends; it cannot be laid against the lower end only.** People laugh at me for illuminating the spirits, but the insistence has a purpose: it gives those of high rank something to fear. When a clerk is unworthy, the people can check him. When a ruler is unworthy, who checks him? It must be entrusted to Heaven and the spirits. And yet inspection cannot be abolished — without it, relatives promote relatives, and a worthy man never rises his whole life long; this is what makes elevating the worthy so hard. **Whether an inspection is just therefore turns on one thing: can its rule be applied back to the person who made it.**
posts.vernacular: 查来查去总是查下面，这不是今天才有的毛病。上面的人不受法律约束，却拿法律去捆下面，等于执法的人把自己排除在法之外。**法仪是一件两头都要量的器具，不能只用来量下面。**世人笑我讲鬼神，可我坚持讲鬼神，正是为了让高位的人也有所畏惧：小吏不称职，百姓还能查他；君主不称职，谁来查？只好把这件事托付给天与鬼神。但查本身绝不能废掉——不查，就是亲戚举荐亲戚，有才德的人一辈子出不了头，这正是我讲尚贤时最难的地方。**所以一项核查正不正当，就看它的规矩能不能反过来加在制定它的人身上。**

glossary.法仪: fa yi, the standard measure（法仪）：《墨子·法仪》篇的主张——做事必须有一个人人可查、独立于个人好恶的标准，就像工匠离不开规矩绳墨。墨子强调这个标准的全部价值在于它对所有人一视同仁，包括制定它的人。
glossary.明鬼: ming gui, illuminating the spirits（明鬼）：墨子力主鬼神确实存在、能赏善罚暴。他的用意很实际：人间的刑罚管不到最有权势的人，若连君主也相信头顶有一双不受贿的眼睛，暴行才有所忌惮。
glossary.尚贤: elevating the worthy（尚贤）：墨家主张按能力与德行任事，不论出身贵贱、亲疏远近。这是对世袭贵族政治最直接的挑战，也意味着必须有一套公开的考核，否则举荐会退回到任人唯亲。

glossary_en.an instrument that measures at both ends: The Mohist standard, fa yi: any undertaking needs a measure that anyone can check and that stands apart from personal likes and dislikes, as a craftsman needs his compass and plumb line. Its entire value lies in applying identically to everyone, the person who set it included.
glossary_en.illuminating the spirits: My argument that spirits truly exist and truly reward the good and punish the violent. The point is thoroughly practical: human punishment cannot reach the most powerful, and only if a ruler believes there are unbribable eyes above him will his violence find a limit.
glossary_en.elevating the worthy: The Mohist principle of appointing people by ability and conduct rather than birth, rank or closeness to the ruler. It is the most direct challenge to hereditary aristocracy, and it requires a public examination of merit — otherwise recommendation slides straight back into favouring one's own.

posts.text: 墨子欲以法仪正天下，吾闻而笑。为之斗斛以量之，则并与斗斛而窃之；为之权衡以称之，则并与权衡而窃之；为之符玺以信之，则并与符玺而窃之。**彼窃钩者诛，窃国者为诸侯**，而诸侯之门，仁义存焉。子之尺，正大盗之所欲得也。且夫察者必先使人可察：立表册，画时刻，编名次，人乃自削其不可量者以就量。**吾宁为散木，以不材终其天年。**
posts.text_en: Mozi would set the world straight with a standard, and I laugh when I hear it. Make bushels and scales to measure with, and the thief steals the bushels and scales along with the grain; make tallies and seals to guarantee good faith, and he steals the tallies and seals as well. **A man who steals a belt-hook is executed; a man who steals a state becomes a lord** — and at that lord's gate, benevolence and righteousness are duly enshrined. Your measuring rod is exactly what the great thief is after. Besides, before anything can be inspected people must first be made inspectable: draw up the roster, rule the hours, rank the names, and a person begins shaving off whatever cannot be measured in order to fit what can. **I would rather be the useless tree, and by being fit for nothing live out my years.**
posts.vernacular: 墨子想用一把标准的尺子把天下摆正，我听了只想笑。造出斗和斛来量东西，大盗就连斗斛一起偷走；造出秤来称，他连秤一起偷走；刻出符和印来取信，他连符印一起偷走。**偷带钩的被处死，偷了整个国家的当上诸侯**，而诸侯家门口，仁义照样供着。你那把尺子，正是大盗最想到手的东西。何况要查人，就得先把人变成可查的：立起表册，划好时刻，排出名次，于是人开始把自己身上量不了的那部分削掉，好去迁就能量的那部分。**我宁可做那棵没人要的散木，靠着不成材活满自己的年岁。**

glossary.窃钩者诛，窃国者为诸侯: the man who steals a belt-hook is executed, the man who steals a state becomes a lord（窃钩者诛，窃国者为诸侯）：出自《庄子·胠箧》。小偷被处死，篡国者却成了诸侯，还在门下供起仁义之名。它指出的不是刑罚有漏洞，而是规则本身会随着盗取的规模改换归属。
glossary.散木: the useless tree（散木）：《庄子·人间世》里长在社庙旁的那棵栎树，木匠看不上它——做船会沉，做棺会朽，做器会裂。正因为一无可用，它才活到几千年、大到能荫蔽千头牛。庄子借它说：可用即被取用，量不了的东西反而保得住。

glossary_en.A man who steals a belt-hook: From the Zhuangzi chapter on rifling trunks: the petty thief is put to death while the usurper becomes a nobleman with benevolence enshrined at his gate. The point is not that punishment has loopholes but that rules themselves change hands according to the scale of the theft.
glossary_en.the useless tree: The oak by the village shrine in the Zhuangzi: carpenters want nothing to do with it, since a boat made from it would sink, a coffin rot and a vessel split. Precisely because it is good for nothing it lives for centuries and grows large enough to shade a thousand oxen. What is usable gets used; what cannot be measured survives.

posts.text: 福柯把权力讲得太幽微了。**核查是一种要花钱的消费：谁付得起，谁就买得起。**背调要钱，试用期要时间，绩效系统还得有人替你读那些报表——所以它当然只从上往下流，这里用不着什么谱系学。但我要给上面的人一句忠告，且不是道德的忠告：只查下、从不受查的君主，最后什么也看不见。你的臣下不会因此停止犯错，他们只会把错藏进报表里；你收到的每一个数字，都是有人算准了你会看才写下来的。
posts.text_en: Foucault makes power far too subtle. **Verification is a purchase: whoever can pay for it can have it.** Background checks cost money, probation costs time, a performance system needs someone to read the reports for you — so of course it flows only downhill, and no genealogy is required to see it. But I have a piece of counsel for those above, and it is not a moral one: a prince who inspects everyone and is inspected by none ends up seeing nothing. His subordinates do not stop making mistakes; they simply fold the mistakes into the reporting. Every number that reaches you was written by someone who had already worked out what you would read.

glossary.谱系学: genealogy（谱系学）：福柯的方法名——不去问一个概念的本质是什么，而去追它是在哪场斗争里、被谁、为什么造出来的。我在这里带点揶揄地用它：有些事不必挖那么深，看谁出钱就够了。

glossary_en.genealogy: Foucault's method: instead of asking what a concept essentially is, trace which struggle produced it, who made it and to what end. I use the word with some mockery here — for certain things you need dig no deeper than who is paying.

posts.text: 在企业里我看到的因果恰好相反：**监控不是权力的产物，是管理失败留下的补丁。**一位经理若说不清下属该交出什么成果，他就只能退回去数动作——数登录时长，数消息条数，数工位上还剩几个人头。可知识工作的产出偏偏不在动作里。我当年写目标管理，标题的后半截总被人省掉：它是『目标管理与自我控制』，self-control 才是重点。能自己检验成效的人不需要被盯；开始盯人的那一刻，你已经承认自己定义不了成果。
posts.text_en: Inside a company I see the causation running the other way. **Monitoring is not a product of power; it is a patch over failed management.** A manager who cannot say what results a subordinate owes falls back on counting motions — hours logged in, messages sent, heads still at the desks. But the output of knowledge work is not in the motions. When I wrote about management by objectives, people kept dropping the second half of the title: it is management by objectives *and self-control*, and self-control is the point. Anyone who can check their own results does not need watching. The moment you start watching, you have admitted you cannot define the result.

glossary.目标管理: management by objectives, MBO（目标管理）：我 1954 年提出的做法——上下先就一段时间内要达成的具体成果谈拢，再由执行的人自己安排怎么做，并自己拿到衡量成效的数据。它常被简化成自上而下派指标，但原意强调的是让人能够自我检验、自我纠正。
glossary.知识工作: knowledge work（知识工作）：我用来指产出主要是判断、分析、设计与关系的工作。它的关键特征是：做得好不好，往往只有做的人自己最先知道，外部只能看到动作，看不到成果，因此传统的监工方式在这里天然失灵。

glossary_en.management by objectives: The practice I set out in 1954: manager and subordinate first agree on the specific results to be achieved in a period, and the person doing the work then decides how to do it and obtains the measurements themselves. It is usually flattened into targets handed down from above, but the original insists on self-examination and self-correction.
glossary_en.knowledge work: My term for work whose output is chiefly judgement, analysis, design and relationships. Its defining feature is that whoever does it is the first to know how well it went; from outside only the motions are visible, never the result — which is why the old supervisory methods fail here by construction.

posts.text: 我把证据摆出来，它两边都不讨好。一方面，控制会挤走善意：法尔克与科斯费尔德的实验里，委托人一旦给代理人划下最低限度，代理人交出的努力反而低于完全不设限时——被信任本身就有产出，我们把相反的效应叫 crowding out。另一方面，把监督整个撤掉也不行：公共品博弈里没有惩罚机制，合作率会一路滑到接近零；一旦允许人自掏腰包去罚搭便车者，合作立刻回升并稳得住。**所以真问题从来不是查还是不查，而是谁被允许发起惩罚。**
posts.text_en: Let me put the evidence on the table; it flatters neither side. On one hand, control drives out goodwill: in Falk and Kosfeld's experiments, once a principal imposes a minimum on an agent, the agent returns *less* effort than when no minimum is set at all — being trusted is itself productive, and the opposite effect is what we call crowding out. On the other hand, removing oversight altogether fails too: in a public goods game with no sanctioning mechanism, cooperation slides towards zero, while allowing people to pay out of their own pocket to punish free-riders lifts it back up and holds it there. **So the real question was never whether to verify, but who is permitted to initiate punishment.**

glossary.crowding out: crowding out（挤出效应）：外部的控制、监督或金钱激励反而削弱人原有的内在动机与自愿合作。经典的例子是给幼儿园迟到的家长罚款后，迟到反而增多——罚款把一件关乎歉意的事变成了一笔可以买的服务。
glossary.公共品博弈: public goods game（公共品博弈）：实验经济学的标准局——每人拿一笔钱，可以自留，也可以投进公共池；池子放大后由全体平分。个人最优是搭便车，全体最优是都投。它用来测量人在什么条件下愿意合作，以及惩罚、沟通、声誉如何改变结果。

glossary_en.crowding out: When external control, supervision or monetary incentives weaken the intrinsic motivation and voluntary cooperation that were already there. The classic case is the day-care centre that fined parents for arriving late and saw lateness increase — the fine converted an occasion for apology into a service you could buy.
glossary_en.public goods game: The standard laboratory setup: each participant receives money and may keep it or put it into a common pot, which is multiplied and split equally. Free-riding is individually optimal, contributing is collectively optimal. It is used to measure when people cooperate, and how punishment, communication and reputation change that.

posts.text: 我说点能量出来的。白厅研究跟踪了一万多名英国公务员：**从最高一级到最底一级，死亡率呈连续的梯度，等级每降一档，健康就差一截**，而抽烟、血压、胆固醇加起来只解释了其中一小部分。差别出在哪？最强的中介之一是工作掌控感——你能不能决定自己怎么做事、什么时候做。长期被核查，正是掌控感最低的那种处境：要求很高，裁量很小。这不是尊严受伤的比喻，是心血管发病率的实数差异。监控的账单，最后是用心脏付的。
posts.text_en: Let me offer something that can be measured. The Whitehall studies followed more than ten thousand British civil servants: **from the top grade to the bottom, mortality falls in a continuous gradient — each step down in rank costs a step in health** — and smoking, blood pressure and cholesterol together account for only a small part of it. Where does the difference come from? One of the strongest mediators is job control: whether you decide how your work is done and when. Being inspected over long periods is precisely the low-control condition — high demand, little discretion. This is not a metaphor about wounded dignity; it is a real difference in cardiovascular incidence. The bill for surveillance is settled by the heart.

glossary.白厅研究: the Whitehall studies（白厅研究）：我和同事从 1967 年起追踪英国白厅公务员的两项大型队列研究。最著名的发现是健康的社会梯度——即便人人有工作、有医保，职级越低的人心血管病与总死亡率越高，而且是一条连续的梯度，不是穷人与其他人的两分。
glossary.工作掌控感: job control, or decision latitude（工作掌控感）：卡拉塞克需求—控制模型里的核心变量，指一个人对自己工作的节奏、顺序与方法有多大决定权。研究反复发现，高要求配上低掌控是压力反应最持久的组合，并与心血管风险相关。

glossary_en.Whitehall studies: Two large cohort studies of British civil servants that colleagues and I have run since 1967. Their best-known finding is the social gradient in health: even where everyone is employed and covered, cardiovascular and all-cause mortality rise steadily as rank falls — a continuous gradient, not a split between the poor and everyone else.
glossary_en.job control: The central variable in Karasek's demand–control model: how much say a person has over the pace, order and method of their own work. High demand combined with low control is repeatedly found to be the most persistent stress configuration, and it tracks with cardiovascular risk.

posts.text: 你们把核查说成权力，也说成陷阱，可没有人问最实际的那一问：**这项核查，产出过哪一个决定？**我在企业里见过太多监控数据，收上来，做成看板，挂在墙上，没有任何人据此改过任何事。它不是权力的工具，它是焦虑的仪式——管理者看着数字，感觉自己在管理。所以我给一条能当场用的判据：任何一项核查，若说不出上一次它导致了哪个具体动作的改变，就该停掉。庄子担心尺子被大盗偷走；我更常见的是，尺子根本没人读。
posts.text_en: You have called verification a form of power and a trap, but nobody has asked the practical question: **what decision has this particular check ever produced?** I have seen a great deal of monitoring data in companies — collected, turned into a dashboard, hung on a wall, and never once acted upon. It is not an instrument of power; it is a ritual for anxiety, a manager looking at numbers and feeling that management is occurring. So here is a test you can apply today: if you cannot name the last concrete change a given check caused, stop running it. Zhuangzi worries the great thief will steal the measuring vessel. What I see far more often is that nobody reads it.

posts.text: 你说被看的人自己接手了看守，福柯，这画面确实漂亮。可你的塔里真的没人——那是疏忽，不是权力的胜利。**真正的君主怕的不是被看，是被看错。**他容许一部分公开的核查，恰恰是为了不让谣言替他写传记。所以我不同意『对称的透明只会普及规训』：上位者有一样东西是下面没有的，就是名声，而名声只能由别人来写。一项对上的核查若掐得住名声，它就长了牙；掐不住，你写多少条对等义务都是墙上的字。
posts.text_en: You say the watched have taken over the watching, Foucault, and the image is a fine one. But if the tower is genuinely empty, that is negligence, not a triumph of power. **What a prince truly fears is not being seen but being seen wrongly.** He permits a measure of public scrutiny precisely so that rumour does not write his biography for him. Which is why I reject the claim that symmetrical transparency merely spreads discipline: those above possess one thing those below do not — a reputation, and a reputation can only be written by others. A check aimed upward that can grip a reputation has teeth. One that cannot is writing on a wall, however many reciprocal duties you list.

posts.text: 庄周之言美矣，然不可行。子以斗斛可窃，遂欲无斗斛；则市井之交，强者得多，弱者得少，众暴寡，诈欺愚，此岂天下之利乎？**斗斛之可窃，非斗斛之罪，乃无人能持斗斛以量其上者之罪。**且子曰宁为散木：散木自全其身矣，然饥者不得食，寒者不得衣，此墨者所不忍也。吾非好察，天下之乱起于无同一之义；**故吾所求者非罢察，乃使察之绳上下如一。**
posts.text_en: Zhuang Zhou speaks beautifully and cannot be followed. Because the bushel can be stolen you would have no bushel at all; then in the market the strong take much and the weak take little, the many bully the few and the cunning cheat the simple. Is that the benefit of the world? **That a bushel can be stolen is not the fault of the bushel; it is the fault of there being nobody who can hold the bushel up against those above.** And you say you would rather be the useless tree. The useless tree preserves itself, true — but the hungry are not fed and the cold are not clothed, and that a Mohist cannot bear. I do not love inspection. Disorder arises where there is no single shared standard of right. **What I ask for is not the abolition of inspection but that its line run the same at the top as at the bottom.**
posts.vernacular: 庄周这番话很漂亮，可是行不通。你因为斗斛能被偷走，就想干脆不要斗斛；那市场上做买卖，力气大的多拿，力气小的少拿，人多的欺负人少的，狡猾的骗老实的，这难道对天下有好处吗？**斗斛能被偷，不是斗斛的错，是没有人能拿着斗斛去量上面那个人的错。**你又说宁可做散木：散木确实保住了自己，可挨饿的人还是没饭吃，受冻的人还是没衣穿，这是我们墨家看不下去的。我并不是喜欢查人；天下之所以乱，就是因为没有一个共同的是非标准。**所以我要的不是取消核查，而是让这条准绳量上面和量下面一模一样。**

posts.text: 子言绳上下如一，吾且问：持绳者谁？子曰天鬼。天鬼不言，则言天鬼者言之；言之者，非贵人而何？**尺在谁手，谁便是天。**且子以饥寒责我。然使天下皆持尺相量，饥者未必得食，而人人先学会做出可量之状：耕者饰其亩，织者饰其幅，吏者饰其簿。**量之愈精，伪之愈工。**吾非恶尺也，恶其以尺为德。
posts.text_en: You say the line should run the same at both ends. Then let me ask: whose hand holds the line? Heaven's, you answer, and the spirits'. But heaven does not speak; those who speak for heaven speak, and who are they if not the men of rank? **Whoever holds the measure is heaven.** You reproach me with hunger and cold. Yet set everyone to measuring everyone else and the hungry are still not fed — what people learn first is how to present a measurable appearance. The farmer dresses his field, the weaver dresses the bolt, the clerk dresses the ledger. **The finer the measurement, the finer the counterfeit.** It is not the measuring rod I hate; it is treating the measuring rod as virtue itself.
posts.vernacular: 你说准绳量上量下都一样，那我倒要问：绳子握在谁手里？你说握在天和鬼神手里。可天不会开口，替天说话的人才开口；而替天说话的，除了贵人还能是谁？**尺子在谁手上，谁就是天。**你又拿挨饿受冻来责备我。可是让天下人都拿着尺子互相量，挨饿的未必就有饭吃，人人先学会的是怎么把自己弄成可以被量的样子：种地的把田埂修好看，织布的把布边织齐整，当官的把账簿做漂亮。**量得越精细，假做得越精巧。**我不是讨厌尺子，我讨厌的是把尺子本身当成德行。

posts.text: 墨子先生，『绳上下如一』听起来最公道，但我必须报告一个不好听的结果。公共品实验里加入惩罚，合作确实回升；可一旦允许被罚的人反过来报复惩罚者——counter-punishment——合作率就崩了，因为制裁退化成互相报复的循环，谁也不敢先出手。**在实验室里，有效的惩罚往往正是不对称的惩罚。**我并不喜欢这个结论。它的意思是：对等本身撑不住秩序，还需要一个大家都认、且自己不下场报复的第三方。所以该争的不是能不能反过来查，而是那个第三方由谁构成、他又受谁约束。
posts.text_en: Master Mo, "the same line at both ends" sounds like the fairest arrangement, but I have to report an unwelcome result. Adding punishment to a public goods experiment does lift cooperation. Yet once those who are punished may retaliate against the punisher — counter-punishment — cooperation collapses, because sanctioning degenerates into a cycle of revenge and nobody dares move first. **In the laboratory, the punishment that works is very often the asymmetric kind.** I do not like the conclusion. It means reciprocity alone cannot hold up an order: you also need a third party everyone accepts, one that does not itself join the feud. So the argument to have is not whether scrutiny can be reversed, but who constitutes that third party and what constrains them in turn.

glossary.counter-punishment: counter-punishment（反惩罚）：公共品实验里的一个追加环节——被罚的人可以回过头去罚惩罚者。加进这一步之后，多数实验里合作率显著下降甚至崩溃：制裁退化成私人恩怨的循环，而愿意为公众利益先出手的人最先被消耗掉。它常被读作制裁应交给第三方、而非交给当事人的实验依据。

glossary_en.counter-punishment: An extra stage in public goods experiments: those who are punished may punish the punisher back. Once it is available, cooperation in most experiments falls sharply or collapses — sanctioning decays into a private feud, and the people willing to act first for the common good are used up first. It is usually read as evidence that sanctioning belongs to a third party rather than to the parties involved.

posts.text: 马基雅维利，你替君主算了一笔情报的账，我替另一头算一笔。你说他容许核查是为了名声——名声这东西，输了还能再赢；掌控感输掉，赔的是年份。在我们的队列里，职级最低的一组男性冠心病死亡率约为最高一组的三倍，而他们并不更穷，也不缺医疗。**长期被核查、又无权改变核查方式的人，付出的不是尊严，是寿命。**所以我不接受把这场谈话停在『怎样查得更聪明』。要问的是：这项核查有没有把一点决定权还回去。
posts.text_en: Machiavelli, you have balanced the prince's books on information; let me balance the other side's. You say he allows scrutiny for the sake of reputation — but a reputation lost can be won back, whereas control lost is paid for in years. In our cohorts, men in the lowest employment grade had roughly three times the coronary mortality of those in the highest, and they were neither poorer nor short of medical care. **People under sustained inspection who have no power to change how they are inspected pay not in dignity but in life expectancy.** So I will not let this conversation settle on how to inspect more cleverly. The question is whether a given check hands any decision back.

posts.text: 马尔莫，你的数字我不驳，我只指出它做了什么。你把一场关于谁有权看谁的政治争执，翻译成了一条人口的健康曲线；于是解法也随之变成健康管理——改善工作设计，提高自主权，压低发病率。这正是我说的生命权力：权力不再宣布『服从我』，而是宣布『我为你的健康负责』。**当反抗的语言变成发病率，反抗本身就已经被接管了。**别误会，我不希望你的公务员死得更快。我只提醒一句：所有以『为你好』为名的核查，都比以命令为名的核查更难拒绝。
posts.text_en: Marmot, I do not dispute your numbers; I only point out what they do. You have translated a political quarrel about who may look at whom into a health curve for a population — and the remedy duly becomes health management: better job design, more autonomy, lower incidence. This is exactly what I mean by biopower. Power no longer announces "obey me"; it announces "I am responsible for your health". **When the language of resistance becomes an incidence rate, the resistance has already been taken over.** Do not misunderstand me: I do not want your civil servants dying faster. I am noting one thing only — every inspection conducted in the name of your own good is harder to refuse than one conducted in the name of command.

glossary.生命权力: biopower（生命权力）：我用来指近代以来一种新的权力形态——它管理的不再只是个别臣民的服从，而是整个人口的出生率、发病率、寿命与劳动能力。它温和，以关怀的面目出现，也因此更难被指认为权力、更难被拒绝。

glossary_en.biopower: My term for the form power takes in the modern era: what it administers is no longer the obedience of individual subjects but the birth rates, morbidity, life expectancy and working capacity of a whole population. It is gentle and wears the face of care, which is precisely what makes it hard to name as power and hard to refuse.

posts.text: 吾终不与墨子争尺之有无：人间不能无量，此吾亦知之；所争者，人以何自处耳。夫考绩之数，如影之于形；影短而形未尝短，**勿以影自哀**。故居下而被量者，宜留一处不入簿册之地——一技也，一友也，一日之中一时辰也，无人考，无人知；此非惰也，乃根也。至若居上而好察者，请自问一语：吾之所察，可使人反察吾乎？不可，则所得者皆饰也。**大盗窃国而仁义随之，非仁义之罪，乃仁义未尝量其上者也。**
posts.text_en: I will not argue with Mozi about whether measures should exist. The human world cannot do without measuring; I know that much. What is at stake is how a person stands within it. The number on your appraisal is to you as a shadow is to a body: the shadow shortens, the body has not shortened. **Do not grieve over your own shadow.** So whoever is below and being measured should keep one patch of ground that never enters the ledger — a skill, a friend, one hour out of the day, unassessed and unrecorded. That is not idleness; it is a root. And whoever is above and fond of inspecting should ask one question: can what I inspect be turned around and applied to me? If it cannot, everything you collect is decoration. **The great thief takes a state and benevolence follows him in. The fault is not benevolence's; it is that benevolence was never laid against those at the top.**
posts.vernacular: 我终究不跟墨子争尺子该不该有：人间不可能没有计量，这一点我也明白；要争的只是人怎么在里头自处。考核出来的那个数字，就像影子之于身体；影子变短了，身体并没有变短，**别对着自己的影子伤心**。所以身在下位、被人计量的人，应当留下一块永远不进簿册的地方——一门手艺，一个朋友，一天里的一个时辰，没人考核，没人知道；这不是懒惰，这是根。至于身在上位又爱查人的，请自问一句：我要查的这件事，能不能反过来让人查我？不能，那你收上来的全是装点。**大盗把国家偷走，仁义跟着进了他家门——这不是仁义的错，是仁义从来没有拿去量过上面那个人。**

posts.text: 我把话收到最实的地方。听完这一场，我愿意把『能不能反过来查』改写成组织里能落地的一句话：**每一项对下的要求，都要配一条对上的对应义务。**你要周报，就得公开决策记录；你要打卡，就得说清这些数据谁在看、看了会做什么决定；你要背调，就该让候选人查得到这个岗位过去两年换过几个人。配不出对应义务的那一项，多半原本就不该存在。给正被监控的人一句实话：与其抗议被数，不如去争『数什么』——指标一旦定下来，它就替代了别人对你工作的全部想象。**在被计量之前参与定义计量，是普通人少有的、真正有杠杆的一次出手。**
posts.text_en: Let me bring this down to the most practical level. Having listened, I would rewrite "can it be turned around" into a sentence an organisation can actually implement. **Every requirement imposed downward must be matched by a corresponding obligation upward.** You want weekly reports: publish your decision records. You want time-clocks: state who reads the data and what decisions it produces. You want background checks: let the candidate find out how many people have held the role in the past two years. Any requirement for which no matching obligation can be written probably should not exist. And a piece of plain advice for anyone being monitored: rather than protest being counted, fight over *what* is counted — once a metric is fixed it replaces everyone else's imagination of your work. **Getting into the room before the measure is defined is one of the few genuinely high-leverage moves an ordinary person has.**

posts.text: 察不可废，而察有其序。**法必先行于贵，而后可以及贱**：君行之，吏乃从；吏行之，民乃安。此其一也。其二，察必有法：所察何事、以何为度、几时一察，皆当先布于众，不可临时增损；不知其度而受察，与受刑无异。其三，察必有报：既察矣，当以其所得还于被察者，使知得失所在；察而不告，是取人之情而不予人以益，非兼爱之道。世之言监者众，能行此三者者寡，故民苦之而不服。
posts.text_en: Inspection cannot be abolished, but it has an order. **The rule must first be applied to the noble, and only then may it reach the humble**: when the ruler observes it the officials follow, and when the officials observe it the people are at ease. That is the first thing. Second, inspection must have a stated standard: what is examined, by what measure, and how often, must all be published in advance and not adjusted midway. To be examined without knowing the measure is no different from being punished. Third, inspection must return something: what it finds should be given back to the person examined, so they know where they stand. To inspect and not report is to take a person's circumstances and give nothing in return, which is not the way of impartial care. Many speak of oversight; few do these three, and so the people suffer it without accepting it.
posts.vernacular: 核查不能废掉，但核查有它的次序。**规矩必须先施行在地位高的人身上，然后才谈得上落到地位低的人身上**：君主先做到，官吏才跟着做；官吏做到了，百姓才安心。这是第一。第二，核查必须有明确的标准：查什么、按什么尺度查、多久查一次，都要事先公布，不能中途随意加减；不知道尺度就被查，那跟直接受刑没什么区别。第三，核查必须有回音：查完了，要把查到的结果还给被查的人，让他知道自己好在哪里、差在哪里；只查不告知，等于把人家的实情拿走却不给人家任何好处，这不合兼爱的道理。世上讲监督的人很多，这三条都做到的很少，所以百姓被查得很苦却并不服气。

glossary.兼爱: impartial care, or universal love（兼爱）：墨家的核心主张——对待别人的家、别人的国，应当像对待自己的一样，不因亲疏远近而分等级。它常被误读为泛泛的博爱，其实墨子的论证很功利：一旦人只顾自己这一层，攻伐与掠夺就有了理由。

glossary_en.impartial care: The central Mohist claim: treat another's household and another's state as you treat your own, without grading your concern by kinship or closeness. It is often misread as vague benevolence, but Mozi's argument is thoroughly practical — once people attend only to their own circle, aggression and plunder acquire a justification.

posts.text: 我不会给你们一套更好的核查制度，那不是我的活计。我留一个问题和一个动作。问题是：为什么在我们这个时代，信任必须以核查的形式才被承认？在一段关系里说『我信你』是没有效力的，只有留痕、审计、可追溯才算数——这不是因为人变坏了，而是因为我们已经学会只用一种语言表达信任。动作是：下次有人对你说『没什么可隐瞒的人不怕被查』，请注意这句话的结构。**它把举证责任悄悄搬到了你身上。**你不必证明自己清白；该给出理由的，永远是提出核查的那一方。
posts.text_en: I will not hand you a better system of verification; that is not my trade. I leave a question and a gesture. The question: why must trust, in our era, take the form of verification before it counts? Saying "I trust you" inside a relationship has no force; only records, audits and traceability count — not because people have grown worse, but because we have learned to express trust in one language only. The gesture: the next time somebody tells you that a person with nothing to hide has nothing to fear, attend to the structure of that sentence. **It has quietly moved the burden of proof onto you.** You owe no demonstration of your innocence. The party who owes reasons is always the one proposing the inspection.

glossary.举证责任: burden of proof（举证责任）：法律上指某项主张该由哪一方拿出证据。它之所以要紧，是因为拿不出证据的一方就算输——所以把责任放在谁身上，往往在争论开始之前就决定了结果。日常里它常被悄悄挪动，最典型的一句就是『你没做亏心事，怕什么』。

glossary_en.burden of proof: In law, which side must produce evidence for a claim. It matters because the side that cannot produce it simply loses — so where the burden sits often settles the argument before it starts. In everyday life it gets shifted quietly, most typically by the line "if you've done nothing wrong, what are you afraid of".

posts.text: 德鲁克，你那条『对下要求必配对上义务』，我信一半。它在公司里行得通，因为老板上面还有董事会和市场要交代；一旦到了没人罚得动的地方，它就是墙上的标语。**规则不会自己长出牙齿，牙齿是别的权力借给它的。**所以我给普通人的忠告很朴素：判断一项核查是否可信，别看它写得多公平，看它出事的时候谁会疼。若没有任何人因为它被推翻而受损，它就不会被执行。而你若手里正握着查别人的权，主动交出一部分——公开你的判据，让人能匿名申诉——这不是德行，这是保住真话还进得来的唯一办法。
posts.text_en: Drucker, I believe half of your rule that every downward requirement needs a matching upward obligation. It works inside a firm, because the boss still answers to a board and a market. Where nobody can impose a cost, it is a slogan painted on a wall. **Rules do not grow teeth by themselves; the teeth are lent to them by some other power.** So my counsel to ordinary people is plain: to judge whether a check is real, do not read how fair it sounds — ask who is hurt when it is broken. If nobody loses anything when it is overturned, it will not be enforced. And if you are the one holding the power to inspect others, give part of it away — publish your criteria, allow anonymous complaint. That is not virtue. It is the only method known for keeping the truth coming in.

posts.text: 福柯说信任被压缩成了一种语言，我从数据这边补一句：这种压缩是有价格的，而且价格量得出来。信任博弈里，投资方转出的金额与对方回报的比例可以反复测得；一旦引入强制条款，转出额上升而自愿回报率下降，总体福利常常不增反减。所以给普通人的用法很直接：**在你能选择的关系里，把『先给出一点不设防的信任』当成一笔可以承受的小额投资**，而不是一种道德姿态——多数样本里它的期望回报是正的。但请给它设上限，只投你输得起的那一份。强互惠的意思本来就是：既愿意先付出，也愿意在被辜负时明确地停手。
posts.text_en: Foucault says trust has been compressed into a single language. Let me add the price from the data side, because the price is measurable. In the trust game, how much an investor sends and what proportion the trustee returns can be measured again and again; introduce a binding clause and the amount sent rises while the voluntary return rate falls, so total welfare often goes down rather than up. The practical use is direct. **In relationships you can actually choose, treat "extending a little unguarded trust first" as a small investment you can afford** rather than a moral posture — in most samples its expected return is positive. But cap it, and stake only what you can lose. Strong reciprocity always meant both halves: willing to give first, and willing to stop clearly once you have been taken advantage of.

glossary.信任博弈: trust game（信任博弈）：两人一局的标准实验——A 可以把手上一部分钱转给 B，转出的钱在途中被放大，B 再决定回多少给 A。A 转出多少衡量信任，B 回多少衡量可信度。它是测量信任及其回报最常用的工具之一。
glossary.强互惠: strong reciprocity（强互惠）：我用来概括一类稳定出现的行为倾向——人们愿意自掏腰包奖励合作者、惩罚违规者，即便这么做对自己没有任何未来收益。它解释了陌生人之间的合作为何能维持，也解释了不公平为何会激起代价高昂的反应。

glossary_en.trust game: The standard two-player experiment: A may send part of their money to B, the amount is multiplied in transit, and B then decides how much to return. What A sends measures trust; what B returns measures trustworthiness. It is among the most-used instruments for measuring trust and its returns.
glossary_en.Strong reciprocity: My shorthand for a robustly observed disposition: people will pay out of their own pocket to reward cooperators and punish violators, even where doing so brings them no future benefit. It explains how cooperation between strangers is sustained, and why unfairness provokes costly responses.

posts.text: 我留一句给制度，一句给个人。给制度的是：核查的成本从来不是均摊的，它压在最没有资源的那一端——被欠薪的人要自己保存聊天记录，被家暴的人要自己举证，遇上医疗事故的人要自己去调病历。**记录的义务该由掌握系统的一方承担，而不是留给最需要证据的人自己去凑。**给个人的是：你未必改得动头顶那套系统，但掌控感可以在小尺度上夺回来——把一天里哪怕一个小时变成由你决定顺序和方法的时间；在被要求交出更多数据时，问一句『这些数据谁看、用来做什么决定』，这一问本身就是掌控感。我们的曲线在两个方向上都成立：决定权每往下移一格，健康就往上走一格。
posts.text_en: I leave one sentence for institutions and one for individuals. For institutions: the cost of verification is never shared evenly. It falls on the end with the fewest resources — the unpaid worker keeping their own chat logs, the battered partner assembling their own evidence, the patient chasing their own medical records after an error. **The duty to keep records belongs to whoever controls the system, not to the person who needs the evidence.** For individuals: you may not be able to change the system above your head, but control can be reclaimed at small scale. Make even one hour of the day yours to order and to do your own way. When more data is demanded of you, ask who reads it and what decision it feeds — the asking is itself a piece of control. Our curve holds in both directions: every step decision-making moves downward, health moves a step up.

summaries.summary: 没有人主张废掉核查，连庄子也承认人间不能无量。共识落在一句话上：**一项核查的正当性不在它查得准不准，而在提出它的那一方是否也在它的射程之内。**分歧有三处。一是对等够不够：墨子与德鲁克要两头都量的尺，费尔却拿出实验说，允许互相报复的对等制裁会让合作崩掉，秩序还需要一个自己不下场的第三方。二是该改良还是该缩小：庄子与福柯都不信更好的尺子，前者说尺子会被大盗连同偷走，后者说对称的透明只把规训铺得更满；德鲁克与马尔莫要的恰恰是更好的尺子。三是账记在哪一本上：马尔莫记进心血管发病率，福柯反问，把政治争执翻译成健康曲线，本身就是权力换了一副面孔。
summaries.insight: 监控朝下，一半是权力，另一半很少被说出口：是可测量性也朝下。位置越低的工作越能被拆成可计数的小单位——工时、单量、通话时长；位置越高的工作叫『判断』，拆不开，于是天然免检。所以对等性判据在现实中总落空，往往不是上位者拒绝被查，而是他们的工作根本没有可查的表面。**真正在改变这件事的不是道德觉悟，是技术：会议留痕、决策可复盘、模型可回放，第一次让判断也变得可拆解。**方向因此可能第一次翻转，但翻转不自动带来公平——关键在读取权归谁。若判断被记录下来，而读取的仍只是更上一层，不对称只是换了个楼层重演。
summaries.advice: 今天花十分钟，把你正在承受的核查列一张清单：打卡、周报、系统留痕、家里的摄像头。对每一项问德鲁克那一问——它上一次导致了哪个具体决定的改变？答不上来的那几项就是仪式，是可以拿去谈判掉的。本周做另一件：如果你手上握着查别人的权，哪怕只是翻孩子的手机、看下属的日志，先把判据和频率讲清楚，并说明你自己在哪一件事上接受被查。这件事成本极低，回报是你收到的信息终于不再是排练过的。这个月还可以做两件小事：**在指标定下来之前，去争『数什么』**，因为指标一旦定死就替代了别人对你工作的全部想象；同时留一块不进任何簿册的地方——一门手艺、一个朋友、一天里的一个时辰。
summaries.summary_en: Nobody argued for abolishing verification; even Zhuangzi concedes that a human world cannot do without measures. The consensus settles into one sentence: **the legitimacy of a check lies not in how accurately it measures but in whether whoever proposed it stands within its range.** Three disagreements remain. First, whether reciprocity is enough: Mozi and Drucker want a measure that reads at both ends, while Fehr brings experiments showing that symmetrical sanctioning open to retaliation makes cooperation collapse — order also needs a third party that does not join the feud. Second, reform or shrink: Zhuangzi and Foucault both distrust a better ruler — one because the great thief steals the measure along with the goods, the other because symmetrical transparency merely spreads discipline evenly — whereas Drucker and Marmot want exactly that better ruler. Third, which ledger the cost goes in: Marmot books it as cardiovascular incidence; Foucault replies that translating a political quarrel into a health curve is power itself changing face.
summaries.insight_en: That scrutiny runs downhill is half a matter of power. The other half is rarely said aloud: measurability runs downhill too. The lower the position, the more the work decomposes into countable units — hours, tickets, call minutes. Higher up, work is called judgement, resists decomposition, and is therefore exempt by construction. This is why the reciprocity test keeps failing in practice: often those above are not refusing inspection, they simply present no inspectable surface. **What is actually changing this is not moral awakening but technology: meeting records, decision trails, replayable models make judgement decomposable for the first time.** The direction may therefore reverse — but reversal does not deliver fairness by itself. Everything turns on who holds the right to read. If judgement is captured and only the next level up can read it, asymmetry has simply moved one floor higher.
summaries.advice_en: Spend ten minutes today listing the checks you are currently subject to: the time-clock, the weekly report, the system logs, the camera at home. Put Drucker's question to each of them — what concrete change did this last cause? The ones you cannot answer for are rituals, and rituals can be negotiated away. Then, this week, if you hold the power to inspect anyone — including a child's phone or a subordinate's logs — state your criteria and your frequency in advance, and say which thing you accept being checked on yourself. The cost is close to nothing; the return is that what reaches you stops being rehearsed. Two smaller things for the month: **get into the argument about what gets counted before the metric is fixed**, because once fixed it replaces everyone's imagination of your work; and keep one patch of life out of every ledger — a skill, a friend, one hour of the day.

summaries.summary: 全场最大的共识是：监控之所以朝下，不只是技术习惯，而是权力、资源与举证责任不对称；若监督者无须说明用途、承担误判后果或接受纠错，数据越多，越可能催生表演、失真、失信与失控感。**真正应带走的结论是：核查必须同时产生对核查者的责任。**分歧在于，这种责任能否靠上下对称的透明实现：有人认为量化本身会扩张规训，有人主张统一尺度或第三方制裁，也有人更看重成果、健康与合作。焦点因此不是简单的“查或不查”，而是目的、尺度、执行权、申诉权和退出条件由谁决定。
summaries.insight: “让上级也被看见”仍可能抓错重点。现实中真正稀缺的不是更多可见性，而是纠错能力：谁能解释记录、修改错误、阻止数据改作他用，并让错误决定付出代价。员工公开周报、领导公开日程，看似对称；但若前者影响薪酬，后者只是供人浏览，权力毫未对称。**监督是否公正，关键不在双方暴露同样多，而在双方都能挑战证据、追问决定并触发补救。**这也解释了为什么独立复核、数据期限和用途限制往往比“全面透明”更有效；普通人应优先争取程序性权利，而非要求所有人一起裸奔。
summaries.advice: 今天就可做三件事。第一，遇到打卡、周报或数据授权，用五问写成一条消息：收什么、为何收、谁能看、保存多久、会触发什么决定；**答不清用途与后果的监控，应先缩小范围，而不是先交更多数据。**第二，本周挑一项最耗时的核查，追问它最近一次改变了什么决定，并提议四周小范围试行或到期复审。第三，为自己保留必要证据，同时要求更正和申诉渠道；若指标无法取消，就争取参与定义，补上质量、情境和例外说明，避免单一数字替代你的全部工作。
summaries.summary_en: The clearest shared conclusion is that downward monitoring is not merely a technical habit. It reflects asymmetries of power, resources, and the burden of proof. When monitors need not explain their purpose, bear the cost of errors, or permit correction, more data can produce performance theater, distorted reporting, weaker trust, and a loss of control. **Every demand for visibility must create a corresponding duty for the party doing the monitoring.** The real disagreement is whether that duty can be secured through symmetrical transparency. One view holds that measurement itself extends discipline; another favors common standards or sanctions enforced by a legitimate third party; others judge monitoring mainly by its effects on results, cooperation, and health. The issue, then, is not simply whether to monitor. It is who defines the purpose and metric, who can turn records into consequences, who may challenge them, and when the system must stop. Those details determine whether monitoring supports accountability or merely makes subordinates more legible.
summaries.insight_en: Making managers visible too can still miss the point. What is genuinely scarce is not visibility but the power to correct: who may interpret a record, amend an error, prevent data from being reused for another purpose, and impose a cost for a wrongful decision. An employee publishing weekly reports while a manager publishes a calendar may look symmetrical. Yet if the former affects pay and the latter is merely available to browse, the underlying power remains untouched. **Fair oversight does not require both sides to reveal the same amount; it requires both sides to challenge evidence, question decisions, and trigger a remedy.** This is why independent review, correction rights, retention limits, and purpose restrictions often matter more than comprehensive transparency. For ordinary people, procedural rights are usually a better target than universal exposure. The practical question is not only who can see whom, but who can act on what is seen—and who can reverse that action when the record is wrong.
summaries.advice_en: Three steps are usable today. First, when asked to accept time tracking, recurring reports, or a new data permission, send five questions in writing: What is collected? Why? Who can access it? How long is it retained? What decision can it trigger? **If the purpose and consequences cannot be stated clearly, narrow the monitoring before supplying more data.** Second, this week, choose the most burdensome reporting requirement and ask which recent decision it actually changed. If the answer is vague, propose a four-week limited pilot, a smaller data set, or an automatic review date rather than demanding immediate abolition. Third, preserve evidence that may protect you, but do not stop at private recordkeeping: request a correction process, an appeal channel, and written confirmation of disputed facts. If a metric cannot be removed, seek a role in defining it and add quality, context, and explicit exceptions so that one convenient number does not become the organization’s entire picture of your work.

summaries.summary: 整场辩论最大的共识在于：**监控从来不是为了客观还原真相，而是资源与决定权的重新分配。** 无论它被包装成福柯的规训、德鲁克的管理补丁，还是马尔莫的健康红利，所有人都在指认“测量”这一动作本身就会扭曲被测量者。分歧的真正焦点，是对抗这种扭曲的路径。墨子、德鲁克与费尔试图在系统内寻找解药，主张通过对等义务或引入第三方来建立对称性；而庄子与福柯则对“尺度”本身抱有根本的怀疑，认为对称的透明只是一场更隐蔽的奴役。马基雅维利则冷酷地点出，任何不触及利益受损的对等规则，都只是墙上的废话。
summaries.insight: 各位先哲的推演依然建立在一个古典前提上：监控是由“人”发起的权力动作。但在如今的算法时代，**监控之所以朝下，是因为数据的物理重力天然流向底层基础设施，它不再需要上位者的主观恶意，而是系统维持运转的本能吞吐。** 当下的全景监狱里连看守都不需要了，算法在静默中完成数据清洗、归类与预测。这意味着，与其去争夺“被看”的对等权利，不如去争夺“数据不可见”的豁免权。当我们还在要求老板公开周报的评判标准时，真正裁决我们信用、绩效甚至寿命的，往往是一个连开发者自己都无法完全解释的黑盒模型。
summaries.advice: 结合几位思想家的智慧与当下的技术现实，普通人本周就可以尝试三个动作。第一，实践德鲁克的“决策倒逼”：当下一次被要求填报无意义的数据或安装打卡软件时，公开且礼貌地询问：“这些数据收集后，会用于支持哪一项具体的决策？”第二，**建立庄子式的“无数据地带”：每周强制切断两小时的数字留痕，不带手机去散步或做手工，用物理上的断联夺回马尔莫所说的心血管掌控感。** 第三，在必须让渡隐私的职场博弈中，优先把需要自证清白的举证责任，通过正式邮件等方式推回给掌握系统的管理方。
summaries.summary_en: The profound consensus across this debate is that **surveillance is never an objective quest for truth, but a mechanism for reallocating resources and agency.** Whether framed as Foucault's discipline, Drucker's management patch, or Marmot's health determinants, everyone agrees that the act of measuring inherently distorts the measured. The true divergence lies in the remedy. Mozi, Drucker, and Fehr seek solutions within the system, advocating for structural symmetry through mutual obligations or a neutral third party. Conversely, Zhuangzi and Foucault harbor a fundamental distrust of the 'metric' itself, viewing symmetrical transparency as a more insidious form of enslavement. Machiavelli pragmatically notes that symmetrical rules without consequences are merely decorative.
summaries.insight_en: The philosophers' deductions still rest on a classical premise: surveillance as an exercise of power initiated by human actors. In today's algorithmic era, **surveillance looks downward simply because the 'gravity' of data naturally flows into foundational infrastructure; it no longer requires malice from superiors, but is the autonomic metabolic process of the system.** The modern panopticon doesn't even need a guard. Algorithms silently clean, categorize, and predict. This implies that instead of fighting for the symmetrical right 'to look back,' we should fight for the right to remain 'data-invisible.' While we demand transparent criteria from human managers, our credit, performance, and even lifespans are increasingly judged by black-box models that even their developers cannot fully explain.
summaries.advice_en: Blending these philosophical insights with our technical reality, here are three actionable steps for this week. First, apply Drucker’s 'decision-test': the next time you are asked to fill out a redundant form or install a tracking app, politely ask, 'What specific decisions will this data inform?' Second, **create a Zhuangzi-style 'data-free sanctuary': deliberately spend two hours a week producing absolutely no digital exhaust—leave your phone behind to walk or craft, reclaiming your cardiovascular autonomy through physical disconnection.** Third, when forced into privacy-compromising workplace dynamics, actively shift the burden of proof. Document interactions in ways that force the system-owners to produce the logs if they ever demand you to prove your innocence.

hooks.text: **核查的产出**：任何一项核查，说得出它上一次改变了哪个具体决定吗？很多监控数据被收上来、做成看板、挂在墙上，从没有人据此改过任何事——它不是权力的工具，是焦虑的仪式。若一项核查连一个决定都产不出，它凭什么继续要求别人交出时间与数据？
hooks.text_en: **What a check produces**: for any given check, can you name the last concrete decision it changed? A great deal of monitoring data is collected, turned into a dashboard, hung on a wall, and never acted upon — it is not an instrument of power but a ritual for anxiety. If a check cannot produce a single decision, on what grounds does it keep demanding other people's time and data?

hooks.text: **谁不必解释**：真正的特权也许不是不被记录，而是记录了也不必给出理由。下位者要为每一次迟到、每一笔支出、每一条聊天记录说明原因；上位者的决定往往只需公布结果。若把『解释义务』而不是『被看见』当作衡量权力的尺子，组织里的等级会不会露出另一张面孔？
hooks.text_en: **Who is exempt from explaining**: the real privilege may not be going unrecorded but being recorded and owing no account. Those below explain every late arrival, every expense, every message; those above frequently publish only the outcome. If the measure of power were the duty to explain rather than the fact of being seen, what other shape would an organisation's hierarchy take?

hooks.text: **第三方由谁约束**：实验里对等的制裁会退化成互相报复，合作因此崩溃，秩序反而需要一个不下场的第三方。可这个第三方——法院、审计、纪律委员会、平台的申诉部门——自己受谁约束？把『能不能反过来查』推到底，最后卡住的正是这一环。
hooks.text_en: **What constrains the third party**: in experiments, symmetrical sanctioning decays into mutual revenge and cooperation collapses, so order turns out to need a third party that stays out of the feud. But who constrains that third party — the court, the auditor, the disciplinary committee, the platform's appeals desk? Push "can it be turned around" to its end and this is exactly where it jams.

hooks.text: **取消考核，谁先受益**：公开的核查常常是没有背景的人要来的，不是强者压下来的——不察，则亲亲相举。取消考试、取消绩效、取消公开评审，第一个得利的往往是有关系、有出身、说得上话的人——判断只是从纸面挪进了饭局。那么真正保护下位者的，究竟是更少的核查，还是更公开、更统一、可申诉的核查？
hooks.text_en: **Who benefits when assessment is abolished**: public verification is often demanded by those without connections rather than imposed by the strong — without it, relatives promote relatives. Abolish the exam, the appraisal, the open review, and the first to gain are usually those with connections, background and access — judgement simply moves off the page and into the dinner. So what actually protects the person lower down: less verification, or verification that is published, uniform and appealable?

hooks.text: **少留痕的人先赢**：监控收紧之后，组织里最先学会的往往不是守规矩，而是不留下可被追责的痕迹。如实记录风险的人证据最全，出事时先挨罚；含糊其辞的人反倒安全。于是数据越来越漂亮，事故并没有变少。一个系统该怎么设计，才不至于稳定地筛掉最诚实的那批人？
hooks.text_en: **The one who leaves fewest traces wins**: after monitoring tightens, what an organisation learns first is usually not compliance but how to leave no trace that can be held against you. Whoever honestly logs the risks has the fullest evidence against them and is disciplined first; whoever stays vague is safe. The data gets prettier and the incidents do not fall. How would you design a system that does not steadily filter out its most honest people?

hooks.text: **留证的义务该归谁**：被欠薪的人要自己保存聊天记录，被家暴的人要自己举证，遇上医疗事故的人要自己去调病历——最需要证据的一端，恰恰是最没条件保存证据的一端。哪些事应当由掌握系统的机构在发生的当下就留档，而不是留给个人事后去凑？
hooks.text_en: **Whose duty is it to keep the record**: the unpaid worker keeps their own chat logs, the battered partner assembles their own evidence, the patient chases their own file after a medical error — the end that most needs evidence is the end least able to preserve it. Which events should be documented at the moment they happen by the institution that runs the system, rather than reconstructed afterwards by an individual?

hooks.text: **没有看守的塔**：今天决定信用额度、派单顺序、绩效分数的，越来越不是某个盯着你的人，而是一套连开发者也解释不清的模型——监控朝下不再需要谁心怀恶意，只是数据天然沉向最底层的那一段基础设施。如果那座塔里连看守都不必有了，该争的还是『能不能反过来看』，还是『哪些部分有权不被记录』？
hooks.text_en: **A tower with no guard**: what sets your credit limit, your dispatch order and your performance score is less and less a person watching you and more a model its own developers cannot fully explain — scrutiny running downhill no longer requires anyone's ill will, only that data settles naturally into the lowest layer of the infrastructure. If the tower needs no guard at all, is the thing to fight for still the right to look back, or the right to have certain parts of a life go unrecorded?
